solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mammal eating mammal, a cold dish

indicators.note: eating means the first mammal takes the second one inside it

parts.note: a cat is a mammal
an ass, or donkey, is a mammal

explanation.surface: A wildlife scene of one creature devouring another, oddly followed by a menu item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like part of 'a cold dish' but supplies the final letter after CASSAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian ice-cream dessert, served frozen, so it is a cold dish.

clue.text: Item climber starting off over slope has on for support?

definitions.text: Item climber starting off over slope has on for support?

indicators.note: starting off means take only the opening letter of climber

parts.note: a ramp is a slope

explanation.surface: A mountaineer puts on a piece of kit before tackling an incline.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' sets C above RAMP; the whole clue describes the spiked plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked attachment strapped to a boot to give a climber grip on ice.

clue.text: Delicate creature, get down dog!

parts.note: to get food down is to swallow it
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: An owner orders a dog off the furniture while a fragile animal watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get down' and 'dog' look like a command to a pet, but are verbs meaning gulp and follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallowtail is a large butterfly, a fragile winged insect.

clue.text: Native American quickly burying head in hands

indicators.note: burying means the word for quickly holds the letter inside it

parts.note: apace means quickly

indicators.note: head in means the first letter of hands

explanation.surface: A tribesman rapidly hides his face in his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: APACE holds H, the first letter of hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are an Indigenous people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Sweet, own scent

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the sweet course
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a perfume as sugary and personal.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for pudding, the course after the main meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a fragrant lotion men apply after shaving, a kind of scent.

clue.text: Killers opening drink a little backward

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the words for opening and sipping from right to left

parts.note: a slot is an opening
to sip is to drink a little

explanation.surface: Murderers start by taking a small, hesitant swig of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns SLOTSIP round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Handguns are weapons that kill, so they can be called killers.

clue.text: Opening left for sailors

definitions.meaning: an opening in a ship's side, as in a porthole
on a ship, the left-hand side is called ...

explanation.surface: A gap is left for sailors to pass through.
explanation.definitionFit: A porthole is an opening in a hull, and nautical usage names the left side port.

clue.text: Veteran comatose as one drags chains in

indicators.note: chains in means these words hold the answer locked inside them

explanation.surface: An old soldier in a stupor hauls his fetters along.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across COMATOSE AS ONE DRAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seasoned is experienced, like a veteran of many campaigns.

clue.text: Sash of brown, indigo tops

indicators.note: tops means the first letter of each word, the top of each in a down clue

explanation.surface: A sash in brown with indigo upper parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' gives a letter too: O, B and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash tied around a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Book half of rabble, as lawman

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: half of means take only the first half of the word for rabble

parts.note: riffraff means rabble

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests half a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is SHE, the H. Rider Haggard novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old West a sheriff was the county law officer.

clue.text: Old commander, on another occasion, dropping in

indicators.note: dropping means the word in is let fall out of the longer word

parts.note: again means on another occasion

explanation.surface: A retired officer pays another visit, popping in once more.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga was a military commander in the Ottoman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ottoman aga was a high-ranking officer, a historical military leader.

clue.text: Modify it with a relevant option

indicators.note: to modify something is to change it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to tweak a choice so that it becomes a more pertinent one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modify' looks like a plain verb asking for ALTER, but it rearranges all the letters that follow it, skipping 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative is another possible choice, a synonym for an option.

clue.text: Fish cutting back, powerfully

indicators.note: back means the word for cutting is turned round

parts.note: a clip is a cutting, as from a newspaper
hard can mean powerfully, as in hit hard

explanation.surface: A fishmonger hacks back at a catch with great force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CLIP into PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Yours truly, a snooty type, reviewed Japanese art

indicators.note: reviewed is taken as re-viewed, looked at the other way, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: yours truly means me, the setter, so I
a snob is a snooty type

explanation.surface: The setter and a haughty critic wrote up an exhibition of Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns I A SNOB round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing miniature trees in pots is a traditional art form from Japan.

clue.text: Start putting on clothes for sport

indicators.note: clothes is read as a verb, to dress or wrap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: putting on a play is showing it
a start is a jump, as from fright

explanation.surface: Advice to begin by getting dressed for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb meaning wraps, not garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Showjumping is an equestrian sport where horses leap fences in an arena.

clue.text: Brewer falsifying report about drink

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the drink
falsifying means the letters of report are distorted and rearranged

parts.note: cola is a drink

explanation.surface: A brewery boss fakes a document about a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsifying' makes PERTOR, which 'about' puts round the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A percolator is a pot that brews coffee, so it is a brewer.

clue.text: Animal wife evidently caught?

indicators.note: evidently says the wife is plainly in the net, so the letter for wife goes inside

parts.note: something caught is netted, so a net

explanation.surface: A spouse seems to have been trapped, like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' gives NET and, with 'evidently', the image of W sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, so an animal.

clue.text: Disappointed only wine available at party then? Daughter going in!

indicators.note: going in means the letter for daughter is put inside the phrase

parts.words: only wine available at party then
parts.note: if only wine is left at a cheese and wine party, the cheese is off the menu

explanation.surface: A guest is let down to find only drink left at the party, as their daughter arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A cheese and wine party with nothing but wine means 'cheese off'; D goes between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for fed up or annoyed, close to let down.

clue.text: Prunes served up, that man in high spirits

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the word for prunes is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to prune is to pare
him means that man

explanation.surface: Dried plums brought to a man in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prunes' is a verb, not the fruit; 'served up' turns PARES into SERAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, celestial beings.

clue.text: Problem with failing, one's fragile

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzling problem
a vice is a failing or fault

explanation.surface: Someone describes a difficulty paired with a weakness, admitting they are delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of china cups and saucers for tea breaks easily, so it is something fragile.

clue.text: Athlete is snubbed by this competitor

indicators.note: snubbed by means the word is is cut away from the word this, leaving its stub

parts.note: a rower is a competitor in a boat race

explanation.surface: A sportsman is cold-shouldered by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' means cut short: THIS loses IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus or javelin thrower is a field-event sportsman.

clue.text: A glass object allowing some light in?

parts.note: a jar is often a glass container

explanation.surface: A glass item, perhaps a window pane, lets in a little light.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as indirect: a door left slightly open lets light through.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open lets a sliver of light past it.

clue.text: Right about costume

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a dress is a costume or outfit

explanation.surface: A judgment on a matter of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is a verb: to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to set it right or remedy it.

clue.text: For example, rose water, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a rose is a bloom, one example of a garden bloom
running water is something that flows

explanation.surface: Rosewater as a garden example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a bloom, and water is a thing that flows, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Charge again, or deal's off

indicators.note: off means the letters of or deal go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: deal's is deal is, the word deal followed by a link

explanation.surface: An ultimatum: pay again, or the agreement is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges OR DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload a gun is to put a fresh charge in it.

clue.text: Line in opera beginning to drift went this way and that

indicators.note: in means the letter for line sits inside the opera's title

parts.note: Salome is an opera by Richard Strauss

indicators.note: beginning to means take just the first letter of drift

explanation.surface: A singer's line in an opera starts to wander off course.
explanation.walkthrough: SALOME holds L after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To slalom is to zigzag down a course, swerving one way then the other.

clue.text: Sign a certain captain has turned up

indicators.note: has turned up in a down clue means the captain's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A notice that a particular captain has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has turned up' turns NEMO round.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of something to come.

clue.text: What almost destroyed west London district

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of what almost are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something nearly wrecked a part of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' makes WALTHAMSTO; 'west' is not a direction here but the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Walthamstow is an area of north-east London, a borough district.

clue.text: Pin on

definitions.meaning: pins is slang for ..., so a pin is a limb
in cricket the on side is also called the ... side

explanation.definitionFit: Pins is informal for the limbs we walk on, and in cricket the on side is the leg side.

clue.text: Odd bits dropping off kitchen freezer?

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters of kitchen leaves the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Bits fall off a kitchen appliance used to keep food cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that frozen water is something that freezes things, not the appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water chills whatever it touches, so loosely it is a freezer.

clue.text: Impressing me, country reversed rule

indicators.note: impressing means the reversed country holds the word me pressed inside it
reversed means the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A dictator wins someone over by reversing the nation's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns NIGER into REGIN, which holds ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a regulated system or programme, a set of rules.

clue.text: He's perhaps right, intellectual artist leaning to the left?

indicators.note: leaning to the left means the pieces run leftwards, read backwards

parts.note: a sage is a wise or intellectual person
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A man of the right, perhaps, is a clever painter with left-wing leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: He is the symbol for helium. 'leaning to the left' turns SAGERAR round.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is an example of a noble gas, one that rarely reacts.
